messages.content: "Could you tell me the estimated date of the Jurassic geological era and calculate how many years ago it was? Also, could you provide the date of the signing of the Magna Carta and calculate how many years ago that event took place?"

function.name: geology_get_era
function.description: Get the estimated date of a geological era. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

era_name.description: The name of the geological era. e.g Ice age

calculate_years_ago.description: True if years ago is to be calculated. False by default

function.description: Get the date of an historical event. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

message.reasoning:
The user wants two things:

1. Estimated date of the Jurassic geological era and calculate how many years ago it was. They want "estimated date" presumably start or end? Usually Jurassic period is about 201.3 million years ago to 145 million years ago. But they might want the start date? We can ask clarifying question: do they want start or end? Or average? Provide both.

2. Date of signing of Magna Carta (1215) and calculate how many years ago.

We need to use the provided functions. For geology_get_era we pass era_name="Jurassic", calculate_years_ago=True. That will return something like {"era_start": ..., "era_end": ...}. Then we can compute years ago from current year 2026? Actually function likely returns years ago relative to present. We'll just trust function output.

For history_get_event_date we pass event_name="Magna Carta signing", calculate_years_ago=True. That returns date and years ago.

We should call each function separately. Use the function calls.
